title: Chicken Jeera
subtitle: Dry-fried chicken thighs with whole and ground cumin
excerpt: Boneless chicken thighs coated in a fragrant, cumin-heavy masala. This is a quick, dry curry with bold spice flavour and very little sauce. Ready in under 40 minutes.
sourceNotes: Anglo-Indian home cooking. Jeera is the Hindi word for cumin, which dominates this simple preparation.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze cooked and cooled portions for up to 2 months. Reheat in a pan with a splash of water.
recipe.batchNotes: Cook in a wide frying pan to keep the chicken dry rather than steaming.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The cooked chicken keeps well in the fridge for 2 days. Reheat gently on the hob.

content.text: Chicken jeera is a dry, fast curry built entirely around cumin. There is very little sauce. Watch the heat closely so the spices toast rather than burn.
Heat the oil in the frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the cumin seeds and fry for 30 seconds until they sizzle and smell toasted.
Add the onions and cook for 10 minutes, stirring often, until golden and starting to catch at the edges.
Add the garlic and ginger. Stir for 1 minute. Add the ground cumin, coriander, turmeric, chilli powder, and salt. Cook for 1 minute more.
Add the tinned tomatoes. Cook on a medium heat for 5 minutes, stirring until the tomatoes break apart and the oil separates.
Add the chicken pieces. Stir to coat in the masala. Cook on a medium-high heat for 8 minutes, turning the pieces so they colour all over.
Lower the heat to medium. Continue cooking for 6 to 8 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce is dry and clinging.
Stir in the garam masala. Taste and adjust salt. Squeeze over lemon juice if using. Scatter with fresh coriander and serve.

items.symptom: The spices smell bitter and sharp.
items.cause: The heat was too high when the spices were added.
items.fix: Add a small splash of water to stop the spices burning, then lower the heat before continuing.

items.symptom: The chicken has released a lot of liquid and is stewing.
items.cause: The heat is too low or the pan is overcrowded.
items.fix: Raise the heat to medium-high and cook uncovered, stirring often, until the liquid evaporates.

items.symptom: The chicken is dry and stringy.
items.cause: It has been cooked beyond the point where the juices run clear.
items.fix: Add 3 tablespoons of water and stir over a low heat for 2 minutes to loosen. Remove from the heat as soon as it is warmed through.
